citations.title: HSBC global insurance business head Moncreiffe to leave, sources say

sentences.text: Under Group CEO Georges Elhedery, HSBC raised its ambition to a 17% RoTE or better in each year from 2026 to 2028, saying it is becoming a simpler, more agile and focused bank, with 1H26 pre-tax profit up 23% to $19.5bn and AI central to the overhaul.

Management moves include Ida Liu as CEO of HSBC Private Bank from January 2026, succeeding interim CEO Gabriel Castello, Cecile Ratcliffe as CEO of HSBC Continental Europe from 1 June 2026, succeeding interim CEO Christopher Davies, and David Rice as first Chief AI Officer from 1 April 2026.

sentences.quote: HSBC's global chief executive for insurance business, Edward Moncreiffe, is set to leave the bank after two decades with the lender

sentences.quote:

sentences.text: HSBC Holdings PLC earns high returns on capital, reporting first-half 2026 profit before tax up 23% to $19.5bn on revenue of $37.7bn, with annualised return on tangible equity of 18.2%.

sentences.quote: HSBC targets RoTE of 17% or better for 2026-2028 (excluding notable items) and year-on-year revenue growth, reaching 5% in 2028 versus 2027. It maintains a 50% dividend payout ratio target basis and now expects 2026 banking NII of at least $46bn.
sentences.text: Management reaffirmed medium-term targets of at least 17% RoTE and a 50% dividend payout ratio through 2028, and guided to 2026 banking net interest income of at least $46bn.

sentences.quote: Capital returns increased: dividends in respect of 1H26 totalled $0.20 per share, with an additional $0.10 interim dividend approved and a new share buy-back of up to $1bn planned.
sentences.text: Capital returns are being rebuilt, with $0.20 per share of dividends for the first half, a further $0.10 interim dividend approved and a buy-back of up to $1bn planned, supported by a CET1 ratio of 14.1%.
The Asia wealth franchise is the main growth engine: wealth fee and other income rose 18%, led by the market-leading Asia business.
Earnings breadth is wide, as all four business segments generated annualised RoTE above 17%.

thesis_pillars.text: HSBC Holdings PLC earns high returns on capital, reporting first-half 2026 profit before tax up 23% to $19.5bn on revenue of $37.7bn, with annualised return on tangible equity of 18.2%. Management reaffirmed medium-term targets of at least 17% RoTE and a 50% dividend payout ratio through 2028, and guided to 2026 banking net interest income of at least $46bn. Capital returns are being rebuilt, with $0.20 per share of dividends for the first half, a further $0.10 interim dividend approved and a buy-back of up to $1bn planned, supported by a CET1 ratio of 14.1%.
